LESSON: SAMSON KILLS A LION

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: The Holy Bible
Topic 2.4: Samson kills a Lion

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Samson kills a Lion. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: How does the story of Samson portray God’s power?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. retell the story of Samson; Judges 14: 5- 9,
2. acknowledge God’s power in his or her life,
3. trust in God to cope with the challenges of life. The learner is guided to: lion’, How does the story of Samson portray God’s power?

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. retell the story of Samson; Judges 14: 5- 9,
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to retell the story of Samson; Judges 14: 5- 9,. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

2. acknowledge God’s power in his or her life,
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to acknowledge God’s power in his or her life,. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

3. trust in God to cope with the challenges of life. The learner is guided to: lion’, How does the story of Samson portray God’s power?
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to trust in God to cope with the challenges of life. The learner is guided to: lion’, How does the story of Samson portray God’s power?. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: At home, obey your parent when they ask you to wash your plate. That shows obedience.

Example 2: Tell the truth if you break a cup. Saying what really happened is honesty.

Example 3: Thank God for your family before you sleep. A short prayer can be: “Thank you God for today.”

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Samson kills a Lion.
2. Explain Samson kills a Lion to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Try this activity: in turns, read Judges 14:5-9,
4. Show that you can: retell the story of Samson; Judges 14: 5- 9,
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Samson kills a Lion. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: How does the story of Samson portray God’s power?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. In turns, read Judges 14:5-9,
2. Model or draw a lion,
3. Sing a song on God’s power,
4. Draw pictures of Samson killing a lion.

SECTION 8: REMEMBER

1. retell the story of Samson; Judges 14: 5- 9,
2. acknowledge God’s power in his or her life,
3. trust in God to cope with the challenges of life. The learner is guided to: lion’, How does the story of Samson portray God’s power?

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.
